messages:
maya: Heads up — need final sign-off on the PRD for the Runtime SLOs & Serving Optimizations initiative. Customers (FinCorp, AdsCo) pushed for stricter latency SLAs: target p99 < 300ms for short gen (<=128 tokens). Draft PRD here: https://redwood.internal/prd/runtime-slo-opt (please review). Main open question: scope — do we include kernel auto-selection + KV cache policy changes in initial launch or split into two phases?

alex: Quick read — thanks. My preference: include kernel-selection *automation* as an opt-in feature in v1, but ship a manual kernel catalog and routing policy first. Fully automated kernel switching can be risky for customer V1s.

jorge: From runtime side: technically we can support both, but auto-selection requires additional telemetry (seq length histograms, kernel perf matrix) and a fallback path when a kernel misbehaves. Also KV cache semantics change with some kernels (sharded vs monolithic). Important edge case: cross-variant cache compatibility when we do rollouts.

sam: Acceptance criteria proposal: 1) Synthetic bench shows p50/p95/p99 improvements vs baseline for targeted workloads; 2) E2E prod traces show p99 <300ms for <=128 tokens on canary traffic; 3) No user-facing increase in 5xxs or generation failures beyond 0.5%; 4) Golden prompt evals (quality) show <1% decrease in automatic metrics or manual review. Need an explicit rollback playbook.

maya: Launch criteria checklist I'm proposing: docs + migration guide, console dashboards (per-model, per-kernel latency, errors, cost delta), automated acceptance tests (bench + golden prompts), canary policy (1% traffic x 48h), and support/ops runbook. Canary failure thresholds: rollback if p99 > baseline + 20% OR error rate >0.5% OR quality regression flagged by eval harness.

alex: On quality: quantization and kernel change might alter logits subtly. We need model-specific eval harnesses with a small but representative prompt set. Suggest we gate auto-kernel for models with A/B eval pass.

jorge: Edge cases to call out in PRD: - long-context mixes (>=4096 tokens) where kernels switch execution path; - KV cache merge conflicts when rolling out new cache TTLs; - prefix-cache poisoning where a cached response is returned for the wrong prompt variant. Proposed acceptance tests: replay production traffic with sequence-length buckets and verify deterministic outputs for non-stochastic modes.

maya: Good. Owners: eng-runtime -> alex (kernel selector RFC) and jorge (cache policy + canary instrumentation). Infra/SRE -> sam (canary config and rollback tooling). PM -> maya (product acceptance + customer comms).

ci-bot: ci-bot: perf job queued: perf/run/1904123456-runtime-prd-bench, expected ETA ~2h. Will post results to the thread once finished.

sam: Also add cost guardrails to launch criteria — unit-token cost impact must be <5% for material workloads or require explicit finance sign-off. Add trace tags and sampling settings for canary to give us detailed flamegraphs.

alex: Drafting RFC for routing + kernel selection. Will include config example and acceptance steps. Example config snippet: 
```yaml
routing_policy:
  priority: latency
  fallback: model-variant-v1
  kernel_selector: auto # options: auto | manual | disabled
  kernel_blacklist: []
  canary_percent: 1
  canary_duration: 48h
```
I'll also add a section on telemetry events we need to emit.

maya: One more ask — product wants to expose a 'performance tier' flag in the API so customers can opt into aggressive optimizations. That would make kernel-auto opt-in simpler. Any objections?

jorge: No objection, but mark it 'beta' and ensure explicit consent documented. We must also document semantic differences (e.g., slight quality/cost tradeoffs).

alex: :thumbsup: will mark auto as opt-in and default to manual in console.

maya: OK — I'll update the PRD to capture these acceptance criteria, edge cases, and owners. Reconvene tomorrow 10:00am to finalize. If anyone strongly objects to including kernel auto-select as opt-in in the initial scope, say now.

jorge: No strong objection, just: please make the fallback deterministic and test it extensively.

alex: Will add deterministic fallback tests to the RFC.

ci-bot: ci-bot: perf job completed — results uploaded to perf/run/1904123456-runtime-prd-bench/results (summary: short-gen p99 improved 18%, long-gen neutral; CPU/GPU utilization within expected bounds). Posting detailed logs shortly.

sam: Nice. Once we have perf logs, I'll sketch the canary SLO dashboard and the rollback playbook.

maya: Thanks all — I'll push PRD updates and ping when the new draft is ready for review.
